endorsements.quote: Across the discussion, panelists emphasized that effective post-market surveillance for modern medical devices requires continuous, context-aware data collection and multi-source RWE.

unlisted_practices: Entrepreneurs should engage with hospital value analysis committees early in the commercialization process.
Ensure post-market surveillance efforts intentionally include pediatric populations.
Understand data flows end-to-end and maintain visibility into third-party dependencies throughout the product lifecycle.
Assume breaches and system failures will occur and plan for them.
Adopt structured risk management frameworks early and incorporate security considerations into design controls.
Map interactions across multiple user personas, including clinicians, patients, caregivers, IT teams, and administrators, to align product design with real clinical environments.
Early-stage AI device teams should focus on a limited set of features addressing clearly defined clinical needs.
Embed regulatory and quality considerations into product development from the earliest stages.
Monitor cost and resource utilization associated with AI deployments.
Review contractual warranties, indemnification clauses, and breach notification requirements as sources of cyber risk.
Foster multi-institutional collaboration and data aggregation to improve safety signal detection for pediatric devices.

screen.reason: Conference proceeding/meeting summary covering considerations, regulatory aspects, and governance/deployment barriers for pediatric software as a medical device and AI.
